Dr Priyank Patel and Dr Shikha Jain have both really helped me come out of my spine issue and I would surely say that they are amongst the best in the country.

⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign
✔️ Progressive weakness or stiffness
✔️ Bilateral upper limb symptoms

🚨 Red Flags Requiring Urgent Referral:
* Bowel/bladder dysfunction
* Rapidly progressive weakness
* Severe gait instability

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
After looking at the 5-star reviews, I visited this doctor for my mother’s left leg pain. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. The doctor is polite in speech but seems very money-minded.

During the first visit, he charged ₹1500 (normal fees), but strongly insisted on getting a Doppler test done through a specific lab. He even called the lab in front of us and mentioned sending the patient directly, which clearly felt like a commission-based referral. This was despite us clearly stating that we wanted to do the test at another known place. He claimed that ultrasounds done elsewhere would not be reliable. The lab he suggested charged ₹6000, while we got the same test done at our known place for ₹5000.

As instructed, we shared the report with him on WhatsApp, but there was no response. Later, my brother personally visited the clinic just to show the reports (the patient was not present). Ideally, this should have been free since it was only for report discussion, but he still charged ₹1000. On top of that, he again recommended another radiologist by sharing a specific name and phone number.

Overall, this was the most money-minded and disappointing experience I’ve had with a doctor.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello! I really feel sorry for patients like you.It is unfortunate that when a correct clinical diagnosis was made and appropriate steps were taken to prevent you from being misled, the response is criticism rather than appreciation. You previously did an incorrect scan elsewhere, which you don't have anything to say about. Now, when a correct scan was suggested after clinical examination, and a correct diagnosis was made, here you are making allegations without even having visited for the follow up consultation and understanding the problem. Let's get the facts clear!

The reason a specific centre was suggested, was to prevent a repeat of an incorrect investigation (like you did before). Prior to consulting me, a venous Doppler had already been done, while your mother’s clinical presentation was not sciatica or venous problem, but strongly suggestive of arterial insufficiency (ischemic pain). A venous Doppler would never diagnose this condition.

The recommendation was therefore for a proper arterial Doppler, done by a senior, reliable radiologist, with whom precise requirements could be clearly communicated. The phone call was made only to ensure the correct study was performed this time — not for any financial reason. I have no commission arrangements, nor do I compel patients to visit any particular center. You were always free to choose where to do the test, which you ultimately did — and the scan confirmed the arterial block, exactly as suspected clinically. (which you should rather appreciate for spot on clinical diagnosis!)

Suggesting accuracy over repetition of wrong tests is called responsible medical practice, not “money-mindedness”.

At no point were you instructed to seek treatment or consultation over WhatsApp. Medical opinions are not given casually over messages.

Your brother later visited the clinic for formal report discussion and guidance, which constitutes a consultation. Doctors do not charge for “presence of the patient” — they charge for professional expertise, time, and responsibility involved in interpreting reports and guiding next steps. This is the same principle by which professionals in any field are paid for their work. Do you or your family members work for free? or ever say to your boss that you don't want payment for a particular month? or a 50% less salary this month would be okay?

If there was any financial difficulty, it could have been communicated. We offer concessions, fee waivers, and charity OPD options for genuinely needy patients. We doctors do that.

It is disappointing that sincere efforts to guide a patient onto the correct diagnostic path are interpreted otherwise. Medicine requires trust in clinical judgment, not assumptions about intent.

I genuinely wish your mother good health. However, when decision-makers are like you who lack trust and respect for sound medical advice, it may indeed be better to continue with whose approach you are more comfortable with and keep on doing investigation after investigations. All the best! 👍🏻
